title: "The Big 3 is all you need to build a good physique"
summary: Attacks minimalism and the dogma that bench, squat and deadlift (or a 'big 5/6') build a complete physique. Using his own case (a 335 lb bench with no triceps, squats that didn't grow his hamstrings, deadlifts that didn't grow his lats), he argues compounds emphasise different muscles per individual and leave biceps, forearms, rear delts, lats, calves and triceps long head underdeveloped. He also rants that powerlifting has a monopoly on YouTube fitness and shouldn't dictate hypertrophy training.

claims.claim: Minimalism is the enemy of a good physique; anyone claiming complete results from incomplete methods is lying or missing something.
Bench, squat and deadlift are not the only or the best compound movements; he likes them because they suit his body type.
Outside powerlifting's dogma of judging strength by three lifts, there's no basis to say the big three are best for developing any muscle.
Depending on individual, stance and grip, compounds emphasise some muscles and may give absolutely no growth in others they supposedly train.
He reached a 335 lb bench with essentially no triceps development; chest and shoulders did all the work.
Squats grew his quads and glutes a lot but did nothing for his hamstrings.
Deadlifts gave him zero lat hypertrophy but a lot of upper back growth.
Even if the big three fully developed their target muscles, biceps, forearms, rear delts, lats and calves would remain undertrained; deadlifts don't build forearms as much as people think.
People preach the big three because of a powerlifting bias that wrongly equates powerlifting with hypertrophy training.
Powerlifting has a monopoly on YouTube fitness and claims to be the best athletic and hypertrophy training without being challenged.
Strongman is a better test of strength than powerlifting: a strongman would do well in a powerlifting meet thanks to squat and deadlift, but a powerlifter would struggle in strongman.
Powerlifters telling bodybuilders how to build physiques is as inappropriate as a bodybuilder telling people how to build strength; everyone should stay in their lane.
He has never seen anyone get a good physique from only the big three, and his own experiment confirmed it.
The big five (adding rows and weighted pull-ups) still leaves the triceps long head, biceps and forearms undertrained.
Overhead press does not give chest development.

A complete physique needs a complete program; bench, squat, deadlift, OHP, weighted pull-ups and rows give good overall development but you still need isolation movements, which the lifting community unfairly hates.
Even muscles the big lifts target may need other lifts: flat bench alone might not suffice for the chest, especially if your shoulders can't take the volume, so use variations and chest isolation.
Don't be dogmatic or fanatic about lifts; apart from a few dangerous exceptions, every lift can be useful when applied properly, and you are the engineer who must experiment.
He made the mistake of training only compound movements and plans to show the physique he had back then.
